name: W merge passes through the crossing
aliases: naturality of the crossing for the W-node
summary: A wire crossing the output of a W merge equals the wire crossing both of its inputs.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The W-node used as a merge (the black monoid: a ternary black vertex followed by a binary black vertex) is an *even* map, so the crossing is natural for it: a wire crossing its output can be moved to cross both of its inputs instead, without a sign. Compare with the odd [NOT gate](../fermionic-crossing-not/) and with the symmetric black vertex, which is odd and [picks up a sign](../fermionic-crossing-w-sign/).
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator

also_in.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $nat_x^w$
